title: Seven trips between two hills
note: The page's seven numbered arrows between Safa and Marwah, odd numbers going, even numbers returning.

lines.text: Sa'i is seven legs between two hills
Safa and Marwah, the tenth of Dhul Hijjah
At Safa, begin with what Allah began with
lines.sub: Safa and Marwah are among Allah's symbols

lines.text: Walk to Marwah: that first leg is one
Seven legs end you at Marwah, not Safa
lines.sub: between the green markers, men jog, a sunnah

lines.text: Sa'i remembers Hajar, alone with an infant
lines.sub: seven times, alone, looking for help

lines.text: Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali: sa'i is a pillar
lines.sub: Hanafis: a duty, a sacrifice repairs it

lines.text: Sa'i is the memory of a woman running
No one walks this Hajj without her path

research.retell: Sa'i is walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwah, retracing Hajar's search for help, and three of the four schools count it a pillar without which the rite fails.
proof: Two hills with seven numbered arrows between them, the odd numbers pointing from Safa to Marwah and the even numbers pointing back.; seven traversals, not seven round trips
The pilgrim of tamattu’ then performs sa’i again, because his earlier sa’i belonged to his Umrah.
The Prophet ﷺ recited, as he approached it, the verse that Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah, and said: I begin with what Allah began with.
Safa to Marwah is one. Marwah back to Safa is two.
Seven ends you at Marwah, not back at Safa.; between the green markers, men jog
Hajar, alone with an infant in a valley with no water, went up one hill and then the other, seven times, looking for help.

Maliki, Shafi’i and Hanbali: sa’i is a pillar; without it the rite is not complete and nothing repairs it but performing it. Hanafi: sa’i is wajib, an obligation; whoever leaves it has a valid Hajj or Umrah and owes a sacrifice.
Sa’i is the memory of a woman running.
so that no one performs this Hajj without walking her path; Umrah, step by step
